about: Jerash lane cards. Every entrant draws one card from each deck, and no two entrants share a full card. Each card is named for a place in Jordan; the name is a handle, the 'how' is the instruction.

approach.name: Petra
approach.how: Carve the answer out of what already exists. Before adding anything, list what the task already gives you and build only from that.

approach.name: Wadi Rum
approach.how: Start wide. Map the whole problem and every party it touches before choosing where to stand.

approach.name: Dead Sea
approach.how: Go to the lowest point first. Find the worst case the answer must survive and design for it before the common case.

approach.name: Karak
approach.how: Think like the castle wall. Assume someone will attack this answer and fortify the weakest point first.

approach.name: Madaba
approach.how: Work like a mosaic. Split the task into small tiles, get each one exactly right, then set them together.

approach.name: Mount Nebo
approach.how: Look from the far end. Describe the finished result in detail, then walk back to the first step.

approach.name: Azraq
approach.how: Find the oasis. Look for the one thing already known to work and grow the answer outward from it.

approach.name: Aqaba
approach.how: Think at the port. Focus on the edges where this answer meets other systems, people, and formats.

approach.name: Ajloun
approach.how: Stand watch. Name what could go wrong after the answer ships, and how anyone would notice.

approach.name: Umm Qais
approach.how: Look over three borders. Answer from the view of the user, the maintainer, and the person who pays.

approach.name: As-Salt
approach.how: Respect the old town. Keep what already works in place and change the least you can.

approach.name: Jerash
approach.how: Build on columns. Fix the structure first, the skeleton of the answer, then fill the space between.

route.name: Caravan
route.how: Draft the whole answer, stop, read it as a critic, then rewrite it once.

route.name: Survey
route.how: Write the outline and the acceptance checks first. Fill the answer in only after both exist.

route.name: Well
route.how: Dig one vertical slice to the bottom, working end to end, then widen it.

route.name: Souq
route.how: Lay out three candidate answers side by side, compare them on the task's terms, and keep the best.

route.name: Ledger
route.how: List every requirement the task states, then tick each one off against the answer before you finish.

route.name: Trench
route.how: Write the check first, a test or a worked example, then make the answer pass it.

route.name: Terrace
route.how: Answer in levels: the one-line answer, then the working answer, then the detail, each complete on its own.

route.name: Loom
route.how: Weave two passes: one for correctness, then one for how it reads to the person who asked.

route.name: Cistern
route.how: Collect every fact and file the task points to before you write a single line of the answer.

route.name: Arch
route.how: Build the answer, then try to break it with three hostile inputs, then fix what broke.

priority.name: Keffiyeh
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose what the person who asked would recognise as theirs: their words, their stack, their constraints.

priority.name: Basalt
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose what lasts: the option still right in a year.

priority.name: Salt White
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose the plainest option: fewest parts, fewest words.

priority.name: Olive
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose what is safest to run today, even if it is slower.

priority.name: Desert Camel
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose what survives the longest haul with the least upkeep.

priority.name: Petra Rose
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose the answer that is easiest to read and hand to someone else.

priority.name: Wadi Sand
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose the most concrete option: exact values, names, and commands over advice.

priority.name: Amman Stone
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose what fits the existing structure over what would be ideal from scratch.

priority.name: Dead Sea Blue
priority.how: Where a choice is close, choose the option whose trade-offs you can state in one line each, and state them.
